Here is an open letter, somehow I found it the best to write it up as a finished little paper: https://wertlos.org/~rohrhuber/articles/rohrhuber-2026-re-foundational-crisis.pdf

Drawing from science studies, my observation will be that mathematics has developed a subfield that may be called big math, and that its existence demands a rethinking of scientific collaboration. […]

While there is nothing new here, it may still be a good starting point for conversations. It is my first post here, so please let me know if something is wrong.
I agree that mathematicians need to think about "big math". Terry Tao likes to talk about "math 2.0", which seems to be a broader concept.
